name: GraphRAG
executive_summary: Builds a knowledge graph from source documents and performs community-based retrieval and summarization. Enables global reasoning over an entire corpus rather than local chunk retrieval.
description: GraphRAG indexes source documents by extracting entities and relationships into a knowledge graph. At query time, it identifies relevant communities (clusters of related entities), retrieves community summaries, and generates a global answer synthesizing across multiple communities. This addresses the "needle in a haystack" problem of standard vector RAG.
when_to_use: Corpus-level reasoning questions (e.g., "What are the main themes across all documents?").
When standard chunk-based retrieval misses cross-document connections.
Complex domains with rich entity relationships (biomedical, legal, technical).
when_not_to_use: Simple factual lookup where standard RAG is sufficient.
When indexing latency/cost for graph construction is prohibitive.
Small corpora where graph structure adds no value.
known_pitfalls: Graph construction quality depends on entity extraction accuracy.
Community detection parameters affect retrieval coverage.
Global summarization can lose fine-grained detail.

primary_source.authors: Edge, Trinh, Cheng, Bradley, Chao, Mody, Truitt, Metropolitansky, Ness, Larson
primary_source.title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization

usage_templates.template:
Source Documents: {{documents}}

Step 1: Extract entities and relationships, build knowledge graph.
Step 2: Detect communities (clusters of related entities).
Step 3: Generate community summaries.

Query: {{query}}

Step 4: Identify relevant communities via graph traversal.
Step 5: Retrieve community summaries.
Step 6: Synthesize global answer from summaries.

variables.name: documents
variables.example: Collection of research papers on climate change.

variables.name: query
variables.example: What are the emerging consensus and remaining controversies in climate modeling?

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: Graph construction is deterministic given fixed extraction prompts. Community detection may vary by algorithm parameters. Query-time retrieval is deterministic.
